## homebridge-xgimi-tv

HomeKit plugin for XGIMI projectors on XGIMI's own firmware (its example names an H1S): KEYPRESSES lines to UDP 16735, power and app launches as hand-written 20000 commands to UDP 16750, and an ICMP ping for the power state · [upstream](https://github.com/fantasytu/homebridge-xgimi-tv) · licence Apache-2.0 · last green `1.3.5`

| Run | Client | Emulator | Runtime | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-01 | 1.3.5 | 1.4.0 | Node 25.8.0 | pass |
| 2026-10-25 | 1.3.5 | 1.3.0 | Node 25.8.0 | pass |

### Coverage by television

#### `xgimi-projector-udp-modelled`

- **discovery**: no API. The plugin has no search; the projector's address is configured.
- **identity**: not written.
- **auth**: no API. The plugin never binds (10000) and so never meets the code on the projector's screen.
- **session**: no API. Every command is one datagram from a fresh socket; there is no connection to keep.
- **keys**: passed 9/9.
- **text**: no API. The plugin has no text command.
- **pointer**: no API. The plugin has no pointer command.
- **voice**: no API. The plugin has no voice command.
- **state**: no API. The plugin reads power from an ICMP ping of the projector's address, which the host the emulator runs on answers, not the emulator.
- **volume**: passed 2/2.
- **power**: passed 2/2.
- **apps**: passed 1/1.

The emulator sent no error status.

## xgimi-home-assistant

Home Assistant integration for XGIMI projectors on XGIMI's own firmware: KEYPRESSES lines to UDP 16735, any other command as a single-quoted 20000 envelope to UDP 16750, and a TCP connect to 554 as its only power-state read; power-on is Bluetooth LE, not on the LAN · [upstream](https://github.com/manymuch/Xgimi-4-Home-Assistant) · licence MIT · last green `d63da2d638ac45f9c11ff38220a889009fd2d9c4`

Not run yet.
